description:
Capture, validate and flush the quick-capture queue at buffer.md, one entry per line.

Subcommands:
  add TEXT — append an UNKNOWN entry; raw capture with no thread, and it fails `tend` until converted
  suggest TEXT [-y] — propose a structured add-* for raw text (INTERACTIVE without -y; prompts to accept or fall back to UNKNOWN)
  add-text THREAD TEXT — append a TEXT entry
  add-ref THREAD TARGET [SUMMARY] — append a REF entry; TARGET is a wikilink target like notes/<stem> or Projects/X
  add-action THREAD TEXT [--due DATE] [--scheduled DATE] [--priority H|M|L] [--depends UUID8] — append an ACTION entry; also reachable as `tasks add`
  list [FILTER] — show the buffer with line numbers, optionally filtered
  rm LINE_NUMBER — remove a single line by its line number
  tend — regroup entries by thread and date, then validate; idempotent
  flush — tend, then write entries into logs/ and clear the buffer

Flags:
  top-level: --quiet suppress info output
  suggest: -y auto-accept the suggestion without prompting
  add-action: --due YYYY-MM-DD applied on flush and ingest; --scheduled YYYY-MM-DD; --priority one of H, M, L; --depends 8 hex chars, repeatable for multiple deps

Examples:
  ["add-action", "Projects/SGB", "(Riaz Arbi) Chase the signed contract", "--due", "2026-06-15", "--priority", "H"]
  ["add-text", "Projects/SGB", "Vendor confirmed the delivery window"]
  ["list"]
  ["flush"]

Notes:
  Prefer the structured add-text / add-ref / add-action commands. `add` writes a deliberately invalid UNKNOWN entry that blocks `flush` until it is removed with `rm` and re-added properly.
  Call `suggest` only with -y; without it, it prompts on stdin.
  Line numbers shift after `rm` and after `tend` regroups — re-run `list` before each `rm`.
  THREAD must resolve to threads/<Kind>/<Name>.md.
  Ordering: buffer add-action, then `flush` to write logs/, then run `tasks` with no arguments to turn ACTION lines into TASK anchors.
  Do not edit buffer.md directly; use these subcommands and `tend` to fix problems.
  Exits 1 on empty text or description, a malformed --due or --scheduled, or a --depends value that is not 8 hex chars.
